spiritual_reading.full_translation:
When the first good that stands forth to order the conflict entered its appointed operation, it entrusted the government of its outward working to a sufficient complement of powers. At the same time, living truth acting from Divine love, together with life-giving wisdom, held the whole ruling force bound in the lowest degree where all things are constrained in suffering and held in forced conjunction. In that state the powers were let down into the outermost plane and intermingled, so that wisdom was entangled with falsity and falsity with wisdom, and each seemed to carry something of the other.

Then living truth from Divine love sent a directed influx to one operative power distinguished by potency, and committed to it the ordering of external truths for use. Afterward living truth itself took those external truths into its own administration, fixed them in their places, and set them up in a higher state of reception under the Divine will. By that ordering it disposed all things, opened a full completeness for the stable arrangement of the whole, and set in order the governing revolutions of general knowledges together with the fullness of organized truths required for the administration of the entire system.

Living truth from Divine love works like wisdom that prepares an ordered form for the indwelling of the Divine end. It distinguishes interior regions and exterior regions within one form of life, assigns each what is needed for harmony, cleanses away what defiles reception, removes whatever disfigures, and arranges goods and truths into a coherent unity, so that when the ruling love comes to dwell, the whole form may honor it by concord and by uses.

Likewise the Divine love that sustains life holds within itself, in wisdom, the complete pattern of what is to be brought forth, before anything is formed in the outermost degree. From that inward pattern it provides the means of discrimination and correction, distinguishes what must be distinguished, removes what is superfluous, straightens what is uneven, and reduces what is rough into a state fit for conjunction. Thus it brings forth a variety of distinct functions in the natural degree, each according to its form, and disposes them for service under one governing end; and what had been unformed becomes fixed and determined by wisdom and skill, then distributed into different uses for the sake of that end.

So it is with the Divine love that sustains life: from wisdom it forms within the complete human pattern all faculties and capacities, each for every service, and it disposes within the lowest degree all illuminations and all other ordered effects, so that when the Divine mediation that unites higher and lower comes in manifest presence, it may dwell within this entire ordered system.

Afterward a final separation is made within that system: whatever is truly living is gathered upward into a clearer state where it can be held in wiser use, while what is merely obstructive and what is falsity is collected together and cast down into the lowest state, where it can no longer injure the ordered whole.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: The chapter reads as a single, coherent spiritual account of how Divine love and living truth order externals, establish stable degrees and governing patterns, prepare a form by purification and arrangement, then separate what is living from what is obstructive. Coherence is strongest in the two extended likenesses (ordering a habitation; forming uses from an unformed state). It stumbles slightly in the catalog of cosmic structures, whose terms appear compressed and fragmentary, but the governing idea—stabilizing and organizing the lower degrees for universal administration—remains consistent.

findings.diagnosis: Coherent substrate setup in correspondential voice. The teaching proceeds by function (mixture/entanglement) rather than by jurisdiction. No narrative seam or administrative inventory appears.
findings.evidence: Text: “the entire ruling-power is entwined and crucified [in the place of mixture;] they were poured out and mixed with each other, the light with the darkness…” The spiritual reading reports only a lexical difficulty (“Crucified” resists a single term) but not a narrative break. The sense arises from function: binding/entanglement in the ‘place of mixture’ explains the spiritual state without needing ranked officers or territorial stations.

findings.diagnosis: Local corruption/condensation rather than an administrative insertion. The paragraph remains mostly correspondential (ordering ‘garments’ = external forms/truths; establishing cosmic architecture as functional ordering), but the end becomes a compressed cosmological catalogue with broken syntax. The spiritual reading ‘stumbles slightly’ here because the text is fragmentary and list-like, not because a different teaching-voice intruded.
findings.evidence: Text moves coherently at first: “called one of his sons… gave to him the leadership of the garments… he hung them and set them up… he set up all things… opened… ten firmaments…” Then it devolves into piled-up items: “the wheel of the stars [the gates of the great firmament,] them and the [twelve signs,].” The reader notes: “catalog of cosmic structures… terms appear compressed and fragmentary, exact mapping… somewhat compressed by the fragmentary phrasing.” This is the classic profile of damage/abridgment: enumerated cosmological features without the connective tissue that would explain their function in the ‘garments’ narrative. Importantly, it is not administrative in the Mani-layer sense: there are no jurisdictional titles, no ranked named powers beyond the already-active Living Spirit, and no ‘authority over X’ governance language—just cosmic components.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential likeness (architect/craftsman) that directly continues ¶2’s functional theme: ordering, cleansing, arranging for indwelling. No sign of overlay or seam expansion.
findings.evidence: Text: “wise craftsman… build a dwelling for the king… divide it up… furnishes… cleans… scrapes away the defilement… arranges them… so that… the king… might glorify him.” The spiritual reading says “The comparison is straightforward,” and uses it to carry the chapter’s narrative forward without forcing. This is archetypal substrate teaching-by-function: preparation/purification → capacity for indwelling.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential likeness (carpenter) with some lacunae but no voice shift. The paragraph teaches by process—conceived form → cutting/separating → removing waste → smoothing → producing diverse implements (uses). Reader unifies broken tool-phrases, indicating minor textual roughness but not insertion.
findings.evidence: Text: “has in his mind the whole form… brings the saw and the adze… cuts… separates… pulls the waste… plane… smooths… produces wooden implements… useful to his master.” The spiritual reading notes “broken phrases… unified,” yet the spiritual sense arises organically from the function of carpentry (discrimination, removal, formation into uses). No administrative markers (no ranks, stations, jurisdiction lists).

findings.diagnosis: Mostly coherent correspondential doctrinal restatement, but with two small seams: (a) abrupt anthropological/cosmic inventory (“limbs… faculties… ships of light… lamps of light… lowest region”) likely reflects textual damage/patchwork; (b) christological/office naming (“Third Ambassador… Mediator of the Light”) is a mild Mani-style identification layered onto an otherwise functional indwelling motif. The reading ‘solves’ this by rendering the figure purely by function, which signals that the name is not necessary to the substrate argument.
findings.evidence: Text: “has [formed the whole likeness] in limbs [all the faculties]… useful [for every service,] the ships of light [and all the lamps of light,]… in the [lowest region,] so that when the great king comes, he who is the Third Ambassador, who [is the Mediator of the Light,] he might dwell in this universe…” The spiritual reading explicitly notes it treated the “Named figure… by function as Divine mediation,” i.e., the narrative works without the proper title. This matches a common seam phenomenon in Mani’s layer: naming an eternal function with an office-title. However, because it is not a standalone administrative block and does not disrupt the flow (it plugs into the ‘king indwells the prepared dwelling’ likeness), the best critical action is to flag rather than excise; removing the title does not meaningfully improve narrative continuity unless one is reconstructing a stricter pre-identificatory substrate.
findings.scope: Annotate the christological/office identification within ¶5: “the great king… the Third Ambassador… [the Mediator of the Light]” as likely secondary naming over a functional ‘indwelling mediator’ motif; also note the surrounding inventory (“ships… lamps… lowest region”) as possibly damaged/patchworked phrasing rather than a deliberate catalogue.

findings.diagnosis: Coherent correspondential conclusion: separation by outcome/function (light gathered upward; waste/darkness cast down). The reader reports no stumble; the ending closes the process-narrative established in ¶1–¶5.
findings.evidence: Text: “The light… will be gathered… and he takes it up to the land; but the waste and the darkness will be gathered and thrown down to the abyss.” The spiritual reading’s conclusion matches the functional sorting motif and does not require administrative machinery (no officers, no territorial governance).

textual_criticism.summary: Findings: 6. Clean correspondential substrate confirmed in ¶1, ¶3, ¶4, ¶6 (no action). Two minor problem areas: ¶2 shows condensation/damage producing a list-like cosmological cluster (recommendation: none, treat as genuine difficulty rather than insertion); ¶5 contains a mild Mani-style naming overlay (“Third Ambassador/Mediator of the Light”) within an otherwise functional indwelling narrative (recommendation: annotate that identification rather than excise). No clear administrative inventory block or excision-worthy insertion is present in this chapter as restored.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: At the time when the F[ir]st [Man of the Greatness arose] he gave the leadership to his five [sons, the five powers: the] Living Spirit and the Mother of Life [in the bond of the lower region,] as the entire ruling-power is entwined and crucified [in the place of mixture;] they were poured out and mixed with each other, the light with the darkness and the darkness with the light.

At that time the Living Spirit called one of his sons, one rich with power. He gave to him the leadership of the garments. Now, he himself [after these things,] of [received the garments from him;] he hung them and set them up [the garments of the powers,] of the Father of Life [in the heights;] he set up all things [by the command] he opened [of the Father of Life;] ten firmaments [for the ordering of the All;] the wheel of the stars [the gates of the great firmament,] them and the [twelve signs,].

⟨p.132⟩ The Living Spirit is like this: Just as [a wise craftsman,] and an architect who might build a dwelling for the king, and divide it up into separate houses and [separate chambers] everything that is required for beauty [and he furnishes in it] and he cleans them. And also the stones [the stains, and scrapes away the defilement from] them for beauty and {loveliness}, and he arranges them and makes them so that should the king come and inhabit that palace, he might glorify him.

Furthermore, the Father of Life resembles a wise and skilled carpenter [who has in his mind the whole form,] before it was worked [as a log,] before it was established and made beautiful and [unshaped,] carpenter [this] works in it, but [first exists] in him in his [thought,] in his understanding, and he brings the saw and the adze, and cuts it into separate pieces [and he separates] it and he pulls the [waste from] it with the {plane} and he smooths it. He shall make many [roughness from] wooden implements, arranging them shape by shape; he cuts and produces wooden implements from it, wooden implements of different kinds, (such as) dishes, bowls. This wood, that [useful] since previously it had not been worked before it was sealed by [ll]ll and wisdom of this dextrous carpenter. He cut it up into different sorts of implements useful to his master.

So is it also with the Father of Life. In his wisdom he has [formed the whole likeness] in limbs [all the faculties] palace [of this great] in it or in a [or in a member] useful [for every service,] the ships of light [and all the lamps of light,] all the other works [and] in the [lowest region,] so that when the great king comes, he who is the Third Ambassador, who [is the Mediator of the Light,] he might dwell in this universe [having come in glory,]

⟨p.133⟩ ... live. The light, however, that is in it [that is gathered out from it will] wise, and he takes it up to the land; but the waste and the darkness will be gathered and thrown down to the abyss.

changes_summary: No changes made. The critic issued no excision recommendations (Findings 1, 2, 3, 4, 6: none). Finding 5 recommends annotation only (no textual modification), so ¶5 remains unchanged.
